surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Cizikas plays his 1,000th game as the Islanders beat the Red Wings
paras: Emmitt Finnie got the scoring started for the Red Wings midway through the first, but Ondřej Palát made it 1-1 for the Islanders midway through the second. Ben Chiarot and Brayden Schenn squared off late in the period. Simon Holmström put the Islanders ahead for good early in the third. Palát struck again with less than seven minutes left to make it 3-1, and that insurance goal turned out to be the winner. Alex DeBrincat cut the Isles’ lead to 3-2, 29 seconds later.

The Islanders drove the play, and the scoreboard caught up. Ilya Sorokin made 18 saves for the Islanders, and John Gibson stopped 18 of 21 at the other end. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Logan Stanley, even without a point, by our Swing measure. The Islanders improved to 11-6-5, fourth in the Metropolitan, while the Red Wings fell to 8-12-3, seventh in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Islanders have points in seven straight games (4-0-3).
Simon Holmström has a point in seven straight games.
The Islanders’ Casey Cizikas played his 1,000th NHL game and had an assist.
The Red Wings have won two of their last ten.
